title: News!
author: Joseph Jacobs
summary: 管家一件件报出坏消息，主人越听越惊，最后连家产也没了。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1894 by G. P. Putnam's Sons; collected by Joseph Jacobs (1854–1916). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: MR. G. Ha! Steward, how are you, my old boy? How do things go on at home?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：哈！管家，你好啊，老伙计？家里怎么样？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Bad enough, your honour; the magpie's dead!
paragraphs.zh: 管家：糟透了，老爷；喜鹊死了！

paragraphs.en: MR. G. Poor mag! so he's gone. How came he to die?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：可怜的喜鹊！它就这么走了。它是怎么死的？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Over-ate himself, Sir.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：吃撑死的，先生。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. Did he indeed? a greedy dog. Why, what did he get that he liked so well?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：真的吗？这贪嘴的东西。它吃了什么这么喜欢？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Horseflesh; he died of eating horseflesh.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：马肉；它吃马肉撑死了。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. How came he to get so much horseflesh?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：它哪来那么多马肉？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. All your father's horses, Sir.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：都是您父亲的马，先生。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. What! are they dead too?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：什么！那些马也死了？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Ay, Sir; they died of over-work.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：是啊，先生；它们是累死的。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. And why were they over-worked?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：它们为什么会累死？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. To carry water, Sir.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：为了运水，先生。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. To carry water, and what were they carrying water for?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：运水？运水做什么？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Sure, Sir, to put out the fire.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：当然是灭火啊，先生。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. Fire! what fire?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：火！什么火？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Your father's house is burned down to the ground.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：您父亲的房子烧光了，先生。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. My father's house burnt down! and how came it to be on fire?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：我父亲的房子烧了！怎么会起火？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. I think, Sir, it must have been the torches.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：我想，先生，一定是火把。

paragraphs.en: MR G. Torches! what torches?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：火把！什么火把？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. At your mother's funeral.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：在您母亲葬礼上用的。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. My mother dead?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：我母亲死了？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Ay, poor lady, she never looked up after it.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：是啊，可怜的夫人，从那以后她就再没缓过来。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. After what?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：从什么时候起？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. The loss of your father.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：从失去您父亲起。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. My father gone too?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：我父亲也不在了？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Yes, poor gentleman, he took to his bed as soon as he heard of it.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：是的，可怜的老爷，一听到那消息就病倒了。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. Heard of what?
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：听到什么？

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. The bad news, an' it please your honour.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：坏消息，恕我直言。

paragraphs.en: MR. G. What? more miseries, more bad news!
paragraphs.zh: 甲先生：什么？还有更多不幸、更多坏消息！

paragraphs.en: STEWARD. Yes, Sir, your bank has failed, your credit is lost and you're not worth a shilling in the world. I make bold, Sir, to come and wait on you about it; for I thought you would like to hear the news.
paragraphs.zh: 管家：是的，先生，您的银行倒闭了，您的信用没了，您在这世上一个先令也不值了。我斗胆来见您，就是为这事；我想您会愿意听听这些消息。
